items.title: 52300_Trummy Young oral history interview
items.q: And naturally, it all ain't going to come out. So, I guess she came there one of those nights when it wasn't working, and she -- she wrote an article in Downbeat... And Earl and Stanley, they kid Helen when they want to kid her now... I just got through talking to him about it.

ctx.x: And when I first started -- when I first went with Earl a lot of people thought I was nuts, some of the things I was playing because guys just weren't playing those kind of things at that particular time, you know. But to me it was a challenge to play. I figured the trumpets and all were playing like that. Why couldn't the trombones play like that way back there then.

So, it was just a different thing altogether. And trombone players didn't play real high anything like that back at that time, and I loved to play high. You know, I was just getting into it. I made a lot of bad notes trying to do it because I remember once, Stanley Dance's wife now --
